description: Committee recommends rezoning 35 properties for higher-density mixed-use.
One property, 117 Avenue P South, requires a land use amendment.
2018 Preston Avenue was removed from the bylaw.

chips.text: Recommended
Staff explained the city's vision to double population and intensify transit corridors.
Residents of Preston Avenue, Ocean Crescent, Grovener Crescent, and Caswell Hill are affected.
Councilors' motions to remove properties from the bylaw were defeated.
Housing Accelerator Fund commitments prevent decreasing density on corridor mixed-use sites.
A resident asked for targeted engagement in Ward 2 before further rezonings.
Multiple residents expressed strong concerns about traffic, parking, safety, and building height.
Councillor Dubois opposed the bylaw due to traffic, parking, and safety concerns on Preston Avenue.
Concerns raised about lower public engagement in Ward 2, a lower-income area.

speakers.name: Traci Baker
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Opt-in Rezoning
said: Describes life in heavy-use Preston corridor area.
Two high schools, senior facilities, market mall create traffic congestion.
Street parking maxed out; alleys used as shortcuts, creating safety hazards.

speakers.name: Diane Sawatzky
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: 120 25th Street West Rezoning
said: City was negligent in securing 120 25th Street West.
CM1 zoning is a substantial change from current RM3.
Concerns about commercial component, traffic, and parking on dead-end streets.

speakers.name: Nancy Coghlan
said: Opposed to CM1 at 2018 Preston due to unique neighborhood conditions.
Area is high-density, constrained two-way street, heavily utilized.
Corridor is single-lane, unlike others with two-three lanes.

speakers.name: Dadmir Afridi
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Opt-In Rezoning for 2018 Preston Avenue
said: Concerned about multi-use opt-in rezoning for 2018 Preston Avenue.
Unaware of multi-use residential/commercial possibility until July 31st notice.
Traffic is unbearable; back alley traffic and crime are increasing.

speakers.name: Glen Royer
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Rezoning on Preston Avenue
said: Moved to Ocean Crescent 25 years ago for peace and quiet.
Infill is causing loss of beauty, quietness, and safety for seniors.
Increased crime, drug use, and unbearable traffic in back alleys.

speakers.name: Jocelyn Zurevinsky
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Rezoning of 2018 Preston Avenue
said: Two blocks around 2018 Preston are already a heavy-use area.
Adding retail space will exacerbate systemic issues like traffic and crime.
Blanket rezoning for six-story buildings pressures infrastructure, changes neighborhood character.

speakers.name: Peta McDougall
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Proposed Zoning Bylaw Amendments
said: Increased vehicle presence and crime raise safety concerns for pedestrians.
Crosswalk near Grovener Crescent is poorly marked, drivers block views.
Cars use alleys as shortcuts, creating bottlenecks and speeding hazards.

description: Permits billboards on city right-of-way at three locations.
Amends zoning bylaw to create a new sign group.
This initiative aims to generate city revenue.

chips.text: Recommended
Municipal Planning Commission raised concerns about traffic safety and visual impact.
Property owners within 150 meters of proposed locations were notified.
Administration was directed by Council to pursue this initiative.
The approach could create future expansion pressure for similar installations.
Municipal Planning Commission questioned if expected revenue justified the change.
Two members of the public opposed the proposal citing safety concerns.
Administration will report back on billboard uptake within 18 months.

description: Rezones 2 hectares in RM Corman Park for a baseball facility.

chips.text: Recommended
RM of Corman Park responsible for potential traffic signal costs.
Councillor Dubois pressed on cost recovery for traffic infrastructure.
Youth baseball players will use new indoor and outdoor facilities.
Unclear if current agreement ensures RM pays for traffic upgrades.
No concerns raised by Stonebridge Community Association or landowners.
Administration working with RM on future cost recovery agreements.
